answer: Memory-hard proof-of-work protects an agent oasis by forcing each candidate node to navigate high-latency memory graphs within a tight deadline, verified by lightweight sparrow auditors. An attacker spinning up fraudulent identities incurs the scarce, non-shareable cost of dedicated physical RAM chips, making zero-marginal-cost replication a fable. However, wealthy adversaries can exploit custom integrated circuits with stacked memory dies to lower verification expenses per identity.
